prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a layered layout: the camera wearer’s hands, the round mixing pan and the long horizontal plank/formwork are nearest in frames 1–2 (roughly 0.2–0.8 m), while the standing person beyond them is about 0.7–1.5 m away; the rebar grid and masonry structure occupy the middle distance, about 0.5–2 m. Across frames 2–4, the viewpoint turns right and downward along the structure, bringing the rebar grid overhead/across the upper view and revealing the wearer’s feet below, while a person remains partly visible beyond or through the grid; in frame 5, a hand and a light-coloured block are again within roughly arm’s reach on the right. Bright regions make near surfaces and limbs easier to separate from the darker ground and background than in RGB, especially where the grid and shadows visually overlap. Exact metric distances are not recoverable from this monocular rendering, and the similar brightness assigned to some connected surfaces, blurred boundaries, and uncertain depth through the rebar make the metre estimates approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map mainly separates several person-shaped regions from a large yellow region spanning the plank/formwork and parts of the masonry structure, showing that people or limbs lie above, beside, and partly behind the structure as the camera turns from left to right. In frame 1, one person region is partly cut off at the lower-left and another occupies the upper-right/centre behind the near pan and plank; later frames contain small or partial person regions near the right side, including an extended arm in frame 4 and a partly cropped person/arm in frame 5. The coloured boundaries make occlusion and partial visibility easier to see than in RGB—for example, where bodies disappear behind the horizontal structure or beyond the rebar—but they provide no dependable metric distance, so only the RGB/depth context suggests separations ranging from arm’s reach to roughly 1–2 m. The map is highly unreliable semantically: the plank or wall is labelled “bench,” a left-side patch is labelled “bird,” several hands and construction surfaces are merged or omitted, and the masks do not establish facing direction or gaze.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, so it supplies no detected body or hand joints and supports no independent estimate of posture, facing direction, gaze, reach, person-to-person spacing, or motion. From this map alone, no person or object can be placed left/right, above/below, in front/behind, or at any distance from the camera wearer. It therefore adds nothing beyond the RGB for resolving limbs that are occluded by the pan, plank, masonry, frame edges, or rebar grid. Its blank output is unreliable for this sequence because people and hands are visibly present in the RGB, including close hands within arm’s reach and partially cropped bodies farther ahead.
